newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. guard has eye trouble after intruder's punch.
newsitem.headline: U.N. guard has eye trouble after intruder's punch.

text.p: A U.N. security guard was suffering from serious eye trouble on Friday after being punched in the face twice by a man trying to enter the United Nations complex on New York's East River.
U.N. spokesman Juan Carlos-Brandt said that the intruder, identified as Vladimir Fontana of the Dominican Republic, was detained by New York police after the incident on Thursday.
The United Nations, he said, would press charges for assault and battery.
The guard, Richard Allyne, 52, of Barbados, was treated and released at a hospital on Thursday for a contusion in his eye but returned on Friday "because apparently it is quite serious," Brandt said.

Fontana, who Brandt said was not connected with the United Nations, had attempted to enter through a gate reserved for U.N. staff and others who have permanent passes. When asked to produce his identification card, he punched Allyne twice in the face. The guard, nevertheless, wrestled him to the ground.
